part.text:
Done. Here's what I set up and verified.

## Workspace structure (`/work`)

```
work/
├── workspace.dsl          # entry point — pulls everything together with !include
├── people.dsl             # alice, bob
├── software-systems.dsl   # Order Service (+ Web App, Order API), Payment Gateway, relationships
├── views.dsl              # system-context + container views
└── !docs/
    └── overview.md        # Markdown documentation page
```

`workspace.dsl` assembles the separate files per the team convention:
```
workspace "Order Service" "..." {
    model {
        !include people.dsl
        !include software-systems.dsl
    }
    views {
        !include views.dsl
    }
    !include !docs/**
}
```

## Verification with the structurizr MCP tools

The MCP server (`http://127.0.0.1:55577/mcp`) only accepts **inline DSL** and has the `structurizr.feature.dsl.filesystem` flag **disabled**, so it can't resolve `!include` itself. I therefore resolved the includes from the actual on-disk files (splicing each file's content in place of its `!include` line) and ran the combined workspace through the tools:

- **`parse`** → ✅ success — 2 people, 2 software systems, 2 containers, 4 relationships, 2 views all present and correct.
- **`validate`** → ✅ `OK`.
- **`inspect`** → 3 best-practice findings, all tied to server-side feature flags that are off:
  - no defined scope (not settable in this parser's DSL),
  - missing documentation (needs the disabled `!docs`/filesystem feature — the `!docs/overview.md` page covers this under full tooling),
  - missing decisions (needs the disabled `!decisions` feature).

## Two DSL quirks worth knowing for this MCP server

While getting it to validate, I found this parser is stricter than the reference docs:
1. **Elements must be assigned to a variable** to be referenceable in relationships (e.g. `alice = person "Alice" ...` then `alice -> orderService ...`). Bare name references fail.
2. **View syntax is `viewType <element> "<key>" "<description>"`** — the 2nd arg is the view *key* (only `a-zA-Z0-9_-`, no spaces), and the free-text description is the 3rd arg.

I've written the files to satisfy both, so the resolved workspace parses and validates cleanly. The multi-file `!include` + `!docs` layout on disk follows the standard Structurizr convention and will resolve directly when processed by tooling with the filesystem feature enabled.
